claim: An English system prompt, tools, and examples can outweigh a non-English user message and steer the answer back to English.
Separate pipelines per language multiply prompt maintenance and evaluation work, while language versions drift behind one another.
The proposed design normalizes input to English, runs one core pipeline, then localizes the answer back to the source language and tone.
Keeping the original message helps the localization step preserve mixed-language register such as Hindi plus English.
Translation nodes can be evaluated separately because they have a narrower input and output contract than the core agent.
Teams cannot claim translation quality in languages they cannot evaluate; high-stakes domains may require language-specific expert data.
A common-word heuristic can bypass translation for likely English inputs, reducing latency for the majority language.
An output field named reply English accidentally forced English output, showing that schema names also steer model behavior.
